doc: Assessments of a requirement document (hierarchical-requirement.fbl#markdown), CRLF endings, read by the rule assessment, which is caseInsensitive (FBL 4.8, 5.1). The four kinds are read in any case: Question, warning, REMARK and idea. The wire value matches a key of the map of kind ignoring case and is kept as written (FBL 5.2, map), and the model holds the enumeration AssessmentKind's key, the stored form Question, Warning, Remark or Idea mapped back to question, warning, remark or idea (DESL 4.4). The checkbox: [ ] reads resolved false, [x] and [X] (line 21) true through the map of resolved, matched ignoring case, and line 20, which leaves it out, reads the binding's default, false (FBL 5.2, default). Line 18's detail is its continuation, the line indented under it, read with its indentation taken off (FBL 4.8, Continuation); an assessment without one reads the empty text. ITEM-0003 holds no requirement, and line 21 is about it: about names an Item or a Requirement through its mentions facet (DESL 4.3). Line 22 is about REQ-0006, which the mark shows was given and since deleted: the assessment is kept as written and reported by std.mentions (FR-039). An assessment has no number: its id is derived from its place among the elements of type Assessment, zero-based (the specification's derived rule, DESL 9.4 positionIn), and is ephemeral. Each edit is followed by its undo, so every edit starts from the input. The first assessment of a file without the section is first-assessment/ beside this one, since a fixture has one input.

steps.doc: An add (the operation addAssessment on REQ-0003, kind question by its default): the rule assessment's insert, place end, container assessments, puts it after the section's last entry, the line span of line 22, which ends at the end of the body, with that sibling's marker - and indentation (FBL 6.2, 6.3, a new item). The emit \[{resolved}\] {kind} {about}: {text} writes literal brackets around the wire value of resolved and the wire value of kind, each the first key of its map whose value matches (FBL 6.2, emit; 5.2, map): the kind question's stored form Question gives Question. The add gives resolved no value; the reading taken is that its placeholder writes the attribute's value, the binding's default false, so the wire value ' ', and the new assessment is open, [ ] (FR-036, FR-037). An assessment has no id of its own: assessment/5 is the one its place derives. The line takes the body's CRLF.
